title.suggested: Tom Allen defeats Bill Davis in 43 rounds at Rhodes' Point

summary.suggested: The Daily Missouri Democrat reported that Tom Allen beat William M. Davis in 43 rounds and 41 minutes on Chouteau Island near Rhodes' Point. Allen and Charley Gallagher then quarreled and a match was made.

metadata.notes: Masthead reads 'Daily Democrat', Wednesday morning, Jan. 13, 1869. Before the 1875 merger, so not the Globe-Democrat. Database still lists the Globe-Democrat.

facts.fact: Allen, born in Birmingham, England, in 1841 by this account (aged 28), had been in the US eighteen months; this was his first fight in this country
Allen beat William M. Davis in 43 rounds lasting 41 minutes on Chouteau Island near Rhodes' Point, about twelve miles above St. Louis; Mike McCoole, Davis's second, threw up the sponge
places: Chouteau Island, near Rhodes' Point, above St. Louis

facts.fact: Standing over Davis in the 40th round, Allen remarked on his opponent
facts.quote: What kind of a fighter is that?

facts.fact: After the fight Allen challenged Charley Gallagher, who had boasted he could whip any man in Allen's corner
facts.quote: You are a coward, and I will fight you in five weeks for $1000.

facts.fact: On the boat back to St. Louis Allen and Gallagher nearly came to blows in the cabin before the crowd kept them apart
A $50 forfeit was put up for Gallagher to fight Allen or Tom Kelley within five weeks for $500 a side

notes: Allen is given as born 1841 here against 1839 in the facts index. Round-by-round [?] marks are transcript uncertainties, not facts. The fight was on shore; the crowd travelled by steamer Henry Adkins.
